note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prostate cancer management following recent biopsy confirmation of persistent ISUP grade group 1 disease.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer surveillance. The patient is a 59-year-old office administrator who lives alone and prefers phone follow-up due to the 90-minute distance from the clinic. He reports no significant lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of 3/35. He is a current smoker with a 26 pack-year history and consumes no alcohol. He performs only chair-based exercises due to limited mobility from osteoarthritis. He is divorced and has a partner who serves as his primary contact. Recent dental check-ups have been biannual. No bone pain or haematuria reported.

Per rectum, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged with a smooth contour and no palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs and no signs of metastatic disease.

admin: Lives >90 min from clinic; phone follow-up preferred where clinically safe.
